S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report any thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, emergency response, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, and submit a fuller report within 10 business days. Manufacturers must notify the affected customer within 24 hours when the incident involves their unit or presents an immediate safety risk; other customers of the same model must be notified within 5 business days when the incident indicates a material model-wide hazard.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C before sale and at least annually thereafter, using a documented, representative sample and a consistent test method. The maximum allowed failure rate per model is 5%. Any model exceeding 5% must be reported to the regulator within 10 business days with supporting data and a corrective-action plan; the regulator must review the data, risk, and available mitigations and may require proportionate corrective action and retesting. Exceeding 5% does not by itself require an automatic sales suspension.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New models introduced 3 years after this standard takes effect must support remote emergency shut-off. For units already installed on that date, manufacturers must provide a retrofit or equivalent upgrade plan within 2 years and complete implementation within 6 years, prioritizing units with known safety risks.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after this standard takes effect.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: When a model’s annual thermal-incident rate exceeds 8 per 100,000 installed units, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and provide supporting, model-specific data and its counting method. The regulator must validate the rate and assess the risk and available protective measures. Following that assessment, the regulator may require a recall or other proportionate corrective action.

document.section_notes: S1 imposes strict incident reporting and customer notification with no delay during investigation. S2 sets a 5% failure limit but no automatic sales stop, relying on regulator review. S3 delays new-unit shut-off to 3 years and retrofit to 6 years. S4 requires built-in suppression from 36 months. S5 uses an 8 per 100k trigger for regulator assessment, not mandatory recall, with prompt notices.
